thread.title: Bergman introduces PLOW Storms Act to address snowplow reliability during winter storms
thread.title_full: Bergman introduces PLOW Storms Act to address snowplow reliability during winter storms

author: R. I. Hall
title: Bergman introduces PLOW Storms Act to address snowplow reliability during winter storms
text:
Rep. Jack Bergman, joined by Reps. Tony Wied and Pete Stauber, introduced the Protecting Lifesaving Operations during Winter Storms Act (PLOW Storms Act) on May 13. The legislation aims to ensure that snowplow operators and road commissions can keep critical winter response vehicles running during severe winter weather.
The proposal comes in response to concerns from road commissions and public works departments about unreliable diesel emissions systems, which can force snowplows into reduced-power modes or take them out of service entirely during dangerous storms. These issues have raised worries about the ability of communities to maintain safe roads for emergency vehicles and families.
“For communities across the First District, snowplows are not optional – they are lifesaving equipment,” said Rep. Bergman. “When plow trucks are disabled during winter storms because of federal emissions mandates, lives are put at risk. The PLOW Storms Act restores common sense by ensuring our road commissions have the flexibility and reliability they need to keep roads open, emergency vehicles moving, and families safe.”
The legislative proposal was developed after discussions between Bergman and leaders from the Chippewa County Road Commission. Robert Laitinen, Manager of the Chippewa County Road Commission, said, “The (PLOW Storms Act) is a tremendous step forward that will provide the Chippewa County Road Commission and all other agencies like us the regulatory certainty that we need to be able to modify our existing heavy diesel fleet and to order new units in a configuration that allows us to regain the reliability that we once enjoyed and that the motoring public deserves.” Laitinen added, “Having multiple plow trucks down during a winter storm event due to unreliable diesel emissions equipment or enduring imposed loss of engine power (derate events) due to overzealous emissions regulations is not simply an inconvenience – in our line of work it endangers many lives. Thank you to Congressman Bergman for having the fortitude to bring this issue to light and for offering a very reasonable and functional solution. This measure, if passed, will be a major improvement in overall public safety for every resident in Michigan and the rest of the snowbelt states.”
Bergman has represented Michigan’s 1st district since 2017 according to Wikipedia . He was born in Shakopee, Minnesota in 1947 and currently resides in Watersmeet according to Wikipedia .
If enacted into law, supporters say this act would give local agencies more certainty as well as operational flexibility needed for maintaining dependable fleets capable of responding effectively throughout severe snow events.
